questions.stem: Which option correctly marks the stressed syllable of principal when it means 'the head of a school'?
questions.explanation: Principal is three syllables with the stress on the first: PRIN-ci-pal. The same first-syllable pattern appears in teacher, doctor and paper. Stressing the middle or last syllable produces a pronunciation English does not use for this noun.

distractorRationale.b: The second syllable is weak, with a reduced vowel
distractorRationale.c: The last syllable is not stressed in this word
distractorRationale.d: Splitting the word and stressing the end still misses the first-syllable pattern

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: Which stress pattern is correct for record when it means 'an official file'?
questions.explanation: The noun record — a file, a disc, a past result — is stressed on the first syllable: REcord. The verb meaning 'to write down' is reCORD. Word class decides the stress in this pair.

distractorRationale.a: This is the verb pattern; the question asked for the noun
distractorRationale.c: Two equal syllables is not how English stresses this word
distractorRationale.d: Both syllables cannot carry the same main stress

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: In the sentence 'The students object to the new rule,' the correct stress is

options.text: OBject — because object is always a noun
obJECT — because here object is a verb meaning 'protest'
ob ject — with equal stress on both syllables
OBject — because it comes after students

questions.explanation: In this sentence object is a verb: the students protest. Two-syllable verbs of this family take second-syllable stress: obJECT, reCORD, conDUCT. The noun OBject would mean a thing, which does not fit the sentence.

distractorRationale.a: Object is a noun in other sentences, but not in this one
distractorRationale.c: English does not give both syllables the same main stress here
distractorRationale.d: Position after the subject does not decide stress; word class does

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: Where does the main stress fall in the word education?
questions.explanation: The suffix -tion pulls the stress onto the syllable immediately before it: edu-CA-tion. The same rule gives inforMAtion and deciSION. Stressing the first syllable of educate does not survive once -tion is added.

distractorRationale.a: That is the stress of the verb educate, not of education
distractorRationale.b: The second syllable is not the one before -tion
distractorRationale.d: The suffix itself is not stressed

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: Which option correctly stresses the compound noun meaning a board that is painted black for writing on?
questions.explanation: Compound nouns in English usually stress the first element: BLACKboard, GREENhouse, FOOTball, CLASSroom. Stressing board would describe a board that happens to be black, not the classroom object.

distractorRationale.a: Second-element stress treats it as adjective plus noun, not as the compound
distractorRationale.c: Leaving both parts unstressed does not mark the compound
distractorRationale.d: Equal stress on both parts is not the compound-noun pattern

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: In which of the following words is the stressed syllable correctly indicated?
questions.explanation: Photography is pho-TO-gra-phy, stress on the second syllable. Photograph is PHOtograph; photographic is photoGRAPHic. The family is a standard illustration that stress moves when suffixes are added, so you cannot copy the stress of the shortest word.

distractorRationale.b: That is the stress of photograph, not photography
distractorRationale.c: The last syllable is not stressed
distractorRationale.d: That pattern is closer to photographic (photoGRAPHic) than to photography

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: Choose the option that has a different stress pattern from the others.
questions.explanation: CONduct, REcord and IMport are all nouns stressed on the first syllable. ConDUCT is the verb, stressed on the second. The odd one out is the verb pattern. Read the gloss in brackets before you choose.

distractorRationale.a: Noun, first-syllable stress — the majority pattern in this set

sources.title: WAEC English Language Syllabus — Oral English

questions.stem: Using the suffix rule, which option correctly stresses nationality?
questions.explanation: The suffix -ity pulls stress onto the syllable immediately before it: natio-NA-lity. The same rule gives aBILity and elecTRICity. Copying the stress of nation (NAtion) is the expected error.

distractorRationale.a: That is the stress of nation, not nationality
distractorRationale.b: Puts the stress on TION, which is not the syllable before -ity
distractorRationale.d: The suffix -ity itself is not stressed
